_note: Segmentation and geography structure of the client deliverable (labels only; taken from the structure of the aftermarket ME workbooks and the definitions document). No numbers live here.
market_name: Global Industrial High Speed Helical Gearbox Aftermarket Market

segments.name: Pumps (High-speed centrifugal pumps (Motor driven & Turbine driven)

oem_geo_aliases.GCC: GCC (Saudi Arabia, UAE, Oman, Qatar, Bahrain, Kuwait)
oem_geo_aliases.Rest of MEA: Rest of Middle East and Africa

2A.name: Country totals, then top-down
2A.stands_for: How big the gearbox aftermarket is in total, in each region and in each country, and how fast each grows.
2A.in_this_market: The global 2025 aftermarket is anchored on the INSTALLED BASE of qualifying high-speed helical gearboxes (OEM unit shipments 2020-25 extended back over the service life, times the share still operating), triangulated with the OEM market x an aftermarket/OEM ratio and with published figures converted to the client scope. That global value is then split top-down: Global -> 5 regions -> South East Asia, MENA and Africa -> 46 countries, each with a share of its parent and a 2025-2032 growth rate set by regional and country analysts (fleet age, utilisation, LNG / gas / petrochemical / power additions, geopolitics). Growth rates are reconciled so countries add up to their region.
2A.produces: Sizing block (share, CAGR, value 2025 per geography); the country CAGR row of the segment-growth band; each country's price level (index) on the ASP sheet; the country total every segment share applies to.

2B.name: Use case x country
2B.stands_for: WHERE the gearbox works - the end-use facility or project that pays for the service.
2B.in_this_market: Each country's 2A total is split by industry vertical: Oil & Gas (one level deeper: Petrochemical, Fertilizers, FPSO and gas pipeline projects, Oil pipeline projects), Power Generation, Cement, Steel, Marine, Others. A segment analyst forms a group view per country group (share and growth premium per vertical with reasons), then country analysts set each country's split. Each transaction belongs to one primary vertical (client allocation rule); vertical growth = country growth + a premium, adjusted so the verticals average back to the country rate.
2B.produces: The 'By Industry Vertical' shares (band 1) and growth rates (band 2) for every country.

2C.name: Product type x application x country
2C.stands_for: WHAT kind of gearbox train it is - the driven machine and the gearbox type inside it.
2C.in_this_market: Applications are the driven equipment: Steam Turbines, Gas Turbines, Compressors (types: Centrifugal and Integrally Geared - IGC), Pumps, Turbo expanders, turbine-driven Blowers. Built bottom-up at global level: installed gearboxes per application x annual in-scope spend per gearbox (parts, overhaul and repair, inspection / monitoring / lubrication, replacement gearboxes, upgrades - each as a share of the new gearbox price). This gives the global application mix, the bottom-up route of the 2A anchor and the base price per application. Country analysts then set each country's application split, with the OEM new-unit mix shown for comparison; types (Centrifugal vs IGC) are shares of their parent.
2C.produces: The 'By Application' shares and growth rates for every country, the global bottom-up sizing route, and the base price per application on the ASP sheet.

strategies.how_they_combine: 2A sets every total. 2B and 2C are two independent ways of splitting the SAME country total (by where the gearbox works, and by what it drives); they are not multiplied together. 2C's bottom-up build also feeds the 2A global anchor and the ASP base prices. In this sheet each number shows what each of the three contributed.
